Troubleshooting, Adaptive Retries & Reproducible Parallel RNG

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting-and-retries.Rmd
troubleshooting-and-retries.Rmd

Overview

Large HPC array jobs fail in predictable ways: a handful of outlier tasks hit OUT_OF_MEMORY or TIMEOUT, shared network filesystems suffer partial writes, or naive parallel seeding silently correlates Monte Carlo replications across compute nodes. This vignette demonstrates how slurmpilot handles all three failure modes deterministically.

1. Adaptive Escalation for OOM and Timeout Failures

When slurm_retry(job, adaptive = TRUE) (the default) inspects failed array chunks:

  • Chunks in OUT_OF_MEMORY automatically trigger --mem escalation (default 1.5x, bounded by max_mem_mb).
  • Chunks in TIMEOUT automatically trigger --time escalation (default 1.5x, bounded by max_time_minutes).
  • Already-completed chunks are never re-executed; their atomic checkpoints remain untouched on disk.
  • Every escalation event is logged in per-chunk retry provenance via slurm_retry_history(job).

Let us simulate a 4-chunk job where chunk 2 suffers an OUT_OF_MEMORY kill and chunk 4 suffers a TIMEOUT kill on attempt 1:

library(slurmpilot)

tmp_root <- tempfile("sp_troubleshoot_")
be <- mock_slurm_backend(root_dir = tmp_root, max_workers = 2L)

res <- resource_spec(n_tasks = 8L, chunk_size = 2L, mem_mb = 512L, time_minutes = 10)
job <- slurm_submit(
  backend = be,
  fun = function(x) x^3,
  args_list = as.list(seq_len(8L)),
  resources = res,
  name = "adaptive_demo",
  seed = 2026L,
  fault_injection = list(oom_chunks = 2L, timeout_chunks = 4L, fail_once = TRUE)
)

st1 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05)
st1$chunks[, c("chunk_id", "state", "attempt", "checkpoint_exists")]
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   chunk_id state         attempt checkpoint_exists
#>      <int> <chr>           <int> <lgl>            
#> 1        1 COMPLETED           1 TRUE             
#> 2        2 OUT_OF_MEMORY       1 FALSE            
#> 3        3 COMPLETED           1 TRUE             
#> 4        4 TIMEOUT             1 FALSE

Calling slurm_retry(job) with zero manual flags detects BOTH failure causes, escalates --mem (512 MB -> 768 MB) and --time (10 min -> 15 min), and resubmits only chunks 2 and 4:

job <- slurm_retry(job)
st2 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05)
print(st2)
#> 
#> ── slurmpilot Job Status: adaptive_demo [COMPLETED]
#> • Progress: 4/4 chunks (100%) | running=0, pending=0, failed=0, oom=0,
#>   timeout=0, cancelled=0
#> • Peak RSS max: 73.4 MB | Cumulative walltime: 0.17s

# Inspect recorded retry provenance
slurm_retry_history(job)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   retry_round timestamp             chunk_id trigger_state old_mem_mb new_mem_mb
#>         <int> <chr>                    <int> <chr>              <int>      <int>
#> 1           1 2026-11-24T21:06:59.…        2 OUT_OF_MEMORY        512        768
#> 2           1 2026-11-24T21:06:59.…        4 TIMEOUT              512        768
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: old_time_sec <int>, new_time_sec <int>, adaptive <lgl>

# Verify completed results in exact 1..8 order
slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE)
#> [1]   1   8  27  64 125 216 343 512

2. Detecting and Healing Corrupted Checkpoints via SHA-256

Every completed chunk writes results/chunk_XXXX.rds atomically (temp file + file.rename()) paired with a cryptographic SHA-256 sidecar (results/chunk_XXXX.rds.sha256). verify_checkpoint() and slurm_collect() validate every digest before deserialization so silent Lustre/NFS truncation or bit rot can never poison downstream inference:

cp2 <- file.path(job$local_dir, "results", "chunk_0002.rds")
verify_checkpoint(cp2, require_sidecar = TRUE)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# Simulate a single corrupted byte on disk
raw_bytes <- readBin(cp2, what = "raw", n = file.info(cp2)$size)
raw_bytes[[length(raw_bytes)]] <- xor(raw_bytes[[length(raw_bytes)]], as.raw(0xFF))
writeBin(raw_bytes, cp2)

# Integrity verifier catches the mismatch immediately
chk <- verify_checkpoint(cp2)
chk$ok
#> [1] FALSE
chk$reason
#> [1] "SHA-256 sidecar mismatch (expected 6fa0d2046e32d048c15fefbb02f016ef94d78444513c64212cb1ee3ad0e7b411, got bfaf6d52f076580f35e12f1dab72e3f378af7ef91ae7e886ca4ad4b4d72ec505)."

# Surgical retry of chunk 2 heals the corrupted checkpoint cleanly
job <- slurm_retry(job, chunks = 2L, adaptive = FALSE)
st3 <- slurm_wait(job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05)
verify_checkpoint(cp2, require_sidecar = TRUE)$ok
#> [1] TRUE
slurm_collect(job, simplify = TRUE)
#> [1]   1   8  27  64 125 216 343 512

3. Reproducible Independent Parallel RNG (L'Ecuyer-CMRG)

Seeding parallel array jobs with naive consecutive integers (set.seed(seed + i)) does not guarantee non-overlapping random-number streams. slurmpilot’s standalone worker.R initializes base R’s L'Ecuyer-CMRG generator and uses parallel::nextRNGStream() (21272^{127} draws between chunks) combined with parallel::nextRNGSubStream() (2762^{76} draws between tasks within a chunk).

You can inspect or reproduce any (seed, chunk_id, task_pos) stream directly via slurmpilot_rng_stream() without mutating your global .Random.seed:

s_c1_t1 <- slurmpilot_rng_stream(2026L, chunk_id = 1L, task_pos = 1L)
s_c2_t1 <- slurmpilot_rng_stream(2026L, chunk_id = 2L, task_pos = 1L)
!identical(s_c1_t1, s_c2_t1)
#> [1] TRUE

rng_job <- slurm_submit(
  backend = be,
  fun = function(i) list(kind = RNGkind()[[1L]], draws = stats::rnorm(200)),
  args_list = as.list(seq_len(6L)),
  resources = resource_spec(n_tasks = 6L, chunk_size = 2L),
  name = "rng_verify",
  seed = 2026L
)
slurm_wait(rng_job, timeout = 30, poll_interval = 0.05)
#> 
#> ── slurmpilot Job Status: rng_verify [COMPLETED]
#> • Progress: 3/3 chunks (100%) | running=0, pending=0, failed=0, oom=0,
#>   timeout=0, cancelled=0
#> • Peak RSS max: 74.0 MB | Cumulative walltime: 0.10s
rng_out <- slurm_collect(rng_job)

# All workers used L'Ecuyer-CMRG and produced empirically uncorrelated streams
all(vapply(rng_out, function(x) x$kind == "L'Ecuyer-CMRG", logical(1L)))
#> [1] TRUE
cor_mat <- stats::cor(do.call(cbind, lapply(rng_out, `[[`, "draws")))
diag(cor_mat) <- 0
round(max(abs(cor_mat)), 3)
#> [1] 0.144

unlink(tmp_root, recursive = TRUE)

4. Production HPC Pre-Flight Checklist

Before submitting a multi-thousand-task job to a university or cloud SLURM cluster:

  1. Audit globals & closures: Run inspect_job_globals(fun, args_list, globals, packages) to catch >50 MB captured closure frames or missing helper symbols.
  2. Profile empirically: Run pilot_run(..., sample_method = "stratified") with 3–5 trials and check pilot$summary$is_heavy_tailed.
  3. Choose chunk strategy: Use strategy = "lpt" in estimate_resources() whenever task costs are heterogeneous.
  4. Dry-run SSH/SLURM staging: Verify the rendered submit.sbatch and Apptainer .def recipe with slurm_ssh_backend(..., dry_run = TRUE).
  5. Preserve checkpoints: Keep results/ and status/ on shared cluster scratch so slurm_retry() recovers partial failures cleanly with SHA-256 verification.
